name: Tool_Durability_Maintenance
description: Tool degradation over use, material-dependent wear rates, repair mechanics with tools and workstations, and maintenance as a gameplay loop.

questions.question: Does tool durability teach real material science principles?
questions.answer: Yes. Different materials wear at different rates: stone chips quickly, iron lasts longer, steel longest. Player learns material choice affects lifespan -- a real engineering principle.

questions.question: Does tool degradation create compelling emergent gameplay moments?
questions.answer: Yes. A tool breaking at a critical moment creates emergent tension and memorable stories. Multi-stage degradation (pristine/worn/damaged/broken) is deeper than binary durability in competitors.

questions.question: Does tool wear feel physically grounded by material interaction?
questions.answer: Yes. Tools degrade based on target: scanning hard rock wears lens faster than soft soil; digging frozen ground wears shovel faster than loam. Wear reflects real physics.

questions.question: Can durability be prototyped in one sprint using existing patterns?
questions.answer: Yes. Durability counter + wear-on-use + visual states + basic field repair can be prototyped in 3-5 days. Uses UE5 health/damage pattern.

questions.question: Is durability system data-driven and extendable?
questions.answer: Yes. Material wear rates, repair costs, degradation thresholds, and visual condition mappings are DataTable-driven. Designer tunes by editing data.

questions.question: Does durability work in UE5.8 without hacks?
questions.answer: Yes. UHealthComponent pattern, surface material system, mesh material swapping -- all standard UE5.8. No engine modifications.

questions.question: Does durability tracking impact performance on RTX 3060?
questions.answer: No. Durability is integer arithmetic per use (negligible). Visual degradation is pre-baked material parameter swap. No runtime cost.

questions.question: Can a colorblind or hearing-impaired player perceive tool condition?
questions.answer: Yes. Visual degradation states use distinct mesh changes (cracks, dents, missing parts), not color alone. Text durability readout when inspecting tool.

questions.question: Does durability have distinctive sound feedback?
questions.answer: v1: wear sounds per use (scratches, creaks), break sound (snap/crackle), repair sounds (hammer clink, file scrape). Achievable with synthetic audio.

questions.question: Does durability syncing work in multiplayer?
questions.answer: v1 is single-player. Multiplayer needs per-player tool state replication. Each player's tool durability is persisted independently.

questions.question: Can community create custom durability behaviors?
questions.answer: Yes. Wear rate tables, repair recipes, and degradation visual sets are data-driven. Modders define unique durability curves for custom tools.

questions.question: Can durability system be localized?
questions.answer: Yes. Condition names, repair instructions, and descriptions use FText. Numerical values (durability %, repair cost) are locale-formatted.

questions.question: Does Tool_Durability_Maintenance depend on Tool_Systems parent?
questions.answer: Yes. Tools must exist before they can degrade. Tool_Systems provides the tool framework and slot system. Durability applies to any tool type.

questions.question: Does durability prove that material science can be a compelling game mechanic?
questions.answer: Yes. Material-dependent wear rates and repair requirements prove real science principles create engaging gameplay, not just educational overhead.

questions.question: Was Tool_Durability_Maintenance derived from Tool_Systems Q10 (degradation)?
questions.answer: Yes. Tool_Systems Q10 asked 'Do tools degrade or need maintenance?' and answered yes. This sub-feature materializes that answer as a concrete durability and repair system.

questions.question: Does durability conflict with accessible gameplay?
questions.answer: No. Durability adds depth without tedium. Auto-repair at stations is available. Player chooses engagement level.

questions.question: What UE5 knowledge is required for durability system?
questions.answer: UHealthComponent pattern, surface material system, mesh component state management. Low-medium difficulty. 3-5 days for core loop.

questions.question: Does this need sub-features?
questions.answer: Not at this level. Future sub-features: Tool_Condition_Visuals, Tool_Repair_Recipes, Workstation_Repair_System.

questions.question: Are siblings missing at this level?
questions.answer: No. Scanner (discovery), Durability (lifecycle), Crafting (creation) form the complete tool system.

questions.question: Is Tool_Systems complete enough for this?
questions.answer: Yes. Tool_Systems confirmed tool degradation, maintenance, and material interactions at DESIGNED status.

questions.question: Should Tool_Durability_Maintenance be built before or after siblings?
questions.answer: Build second, after Scanner_Tool_Implementation. Scanner gives a concrete tool to test durability on.

questions.question: What does durability block?
questions.answer: Blocks crafting system (crafting produces tools that need durability). Does not block scanner.

questions.question: Does durability system serve the educational RPG goal?
questions.answer: Yes. Durability teaches material science, entropy, and preventative maintenance. Every broken and repaired tool is a lesson in real materials behavior.

questions.question: What is sacrificed by building durability now?
questions.answer: Durability adds complexity to every tool interaction. Risk mitigated by: auto-repair stations, clear visual feedback, and educational framing.

questions.question: What evidence shows durability systems improve games?
questions.answer: Zelda: Breath of the Wild's weapon durability proved breakable tools create emergent gameplay. Minecraft's tool durability is a core engagement loop.

questions.question: Does durability chain reach a human learning something real?
questions.answer: Yes. Player learns: wear rates depend on material hardness vs. target, preventative maintenance is more efficient than reactive repair.

questions.question: How does tool degradation create recurring demand for repair materials, forming a secondary maintenance economy that affects long-term tool total cost of ownership?
questions.answer: Durability shapes the tool market. A stone pick lasts 10 hours (free to craft but replacement every 2 sessions). An iron pick lasts 50 hours (50 credits, replacement every 10 sessions). Steel lasts 200 hours (300 credits, every 40 sessions). Total cost of ownership favors steel at 4 credits/hour vs. stone at 5. Players who repair at 80% wear spend 60% less on replacement than those who use tools to destruction.

questions.question: Does tool wear and maintenance tell the story of equipment with a history — scratches on the scanner from a fall, patched hull plates, a favorite tool repaired so many times it has become unique?
questions.answer: A worn tool tells a story of use: the cracked screen is from that crash, the dented casing is from that creature, the replaced handle is from that long trek — every repair is a scar with a memory.

questions.question: Does the player receive clear, non-intrusive warnings before a tool breaks, and is repair accessible enough that maintenance feels like planning rather than punishment?
questions.answer: Tool durability shows as a segmented bar (5 segments). At 1 segment remaining: subtle pulsing red icon. Breaking: screen-edge crack effect + sound. Repair requires same material as tool + a workbench within 50m. Repair cost = 30% of craft cost.

questions.question: Does each tool's current durability, quality modifiers, and repair history need to persist?
questions.answer: Yes. Each tool item stores: current durability (float 0-100), max durability (float, affected by material quality), repair count (integer, each repair slightly reduces max durability), and quality modifiers. Written on tool use or repair. Frequent writes during gameplay.

questions.question: Does tool wear model real material fatigue (stress cycles, work hardening, crack propagation) or is it a linear degradation curve?
questions.answer: Linear degradation per use with a quality multiplier. No material fatigue simulation. Higher-quality tools degrade slower (lower linear rate) and can be repaired more times. The educational connection is explained textually rather than simulated.
